justifications.durability: the renames are committed fragment data, and the composed-record id audit that runs at check-manifest and audit-doc at closure is the ongoing guard that catches a re-introduced bare colliding id; the landing record is committed. Weaker than the code arm: no committed test asserts these 23 base collisions stay gone or pins the rename convention, so the rename's only regression guard is the generic composition audit, and the verification helpers (rename_ids.py, verify_rename.py, check_links.py) live in the run directory rather than the tree.
justifications.evidence: strong: two gate arms with logs that name revision, tree, module and cwd; independently reproduced by materialising the three directories' bytes at 07ad28145 and 0fda5bbef into a scratch tree under TMPDIR and running the audit via the module the reviewed run names — base 23 findings EXIT=1, head 0 findings EXIT=0, matching the run's logs; the attribute-only claim, the stem-prefix convention and the previously-colliding condition were re-derived file by file against the run's own bytes (30 files, 107 renames, no problem but the expected new landing fragment); the repo-wide remainder of 46 findings was reproduced exactly. Two caveats, neither affecting the renamed ids: the manifest's baseline_suite/after_suite are empty because the node ran audit arms rather than a pytest suite (correct for a docs-only change, but a reader must fall back to the audit logs for the arm figures), and check_links.py drops a same-file bare anchor outside the node directories (docs/evidence/archive/flight-control-config-landed.html#provenance), so its 'elsewhere' list under-reports by one — no link into a renamed fragment exists either way.
justifications.fit: the rename convention follows the already-prefixed fragments elsewhere (new id = fragment file stem + '-' + old id), which is the node id, so a sibling fragment composed into one record cannot claim the same anchor; the landing record is placed in the plan directory the id-prefix rule belongs to and carries no element ids, so it adds none to the composition it is checked by; the change reuses the existing reckon.doccheck.audit_fragment_ids rather than introducing a new check.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node goal is the rename half of crew-observability-truth section 40: the pre-existing bare-id collisions in committed fragments are renamed under their node ids, plan by plan, so each composed record audits clean. Commit 5c4da26fb prefixes 107 colliding element ids across the 30 committed fragments of the a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking, crew-observability-truth and scoring-should-stop-a-promotion directories; audit_fragment_ids reads 0 findings over the three directories at head 0fda5bbef where it read 23 (9+8+6) at base 07ad28145, reproduced independently.
justifications.scope_discipline: commit 5c4da26fb changes only the 30 fragment files and commit 0fda5bbef adds only docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/fragment-ids-renamed-batch-b.html; all 31 changed paths are in the manifest's changed_paths. Conventional subjects with bodies; no plan HTML, plan state, index or sprint file touched. The declared write path docs/figures/crew-observability-truth/fragment-ids-renamed-batch-b was not written (the done-when names no figure), which is an unused declaration rather than an out-of-scope change.
